title.purpose: The product name at the top of the rail. Largest type on the screen.

headline.purpose: Dock heading: ticket name or the summon title.

body.purpose: Base size: tally, control text, messages. 500 for button labels and ticket names, 600 on the primary button.

label.purpose: Field and segment labels in the dock; dock notes and the stage hint at 400.

caption.purpose: Row meta, dock meta, hints; 500 for roster group headings; tabular figures for elapsed time.

chip.purpose: Overhead chips and the status pill; 600 when asking.

terminal.purpose: JetBrains Mono inside the xterm well only.

shadows.name: chip-rest
shadows.purpose: Every overhead chip, lifting it off the paving.

shadows.name: chip-raised
shadows.purpose: Hovered chip, or the chip of the agent open in the dock.

shadows.name: petition-pulse
shadows.purpose: Glaze ring that keeps leaving an asking chip, layered over chip-rest.

shadows.name: dock-overlay
shadows.purpose: Only at 1100px and below, when the dock covers the stage.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one easing for every shell transition (--ease-out).

motion.name: state-change
motion.purpose: Background, border, colour and shadow transitions.

motion.name: petition
motion.purpose: Asking chip pulse. The only looping animation; removed under reduced motion.

motion.name: figure-walk

motion.name: figure-run

components.css: .ds-chip-stage { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 1rem; padding: 1.5rem; background: var(--mist); } .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.375rem; padding: 0.25rem 0.625rem 0.25rem 0.5rem; border: 0; border-radius: 999px; font: 500 0.75rem/1.3 var(--font-ui, "Be Vietnam Pro", system-ui, sans-serif); white-space: nowrap; max-width: 13rem; background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--ink) 88%, transparent); color: var(--bone); cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px oklch(0.2 0.02 40 / 0.28); transition: background-color 160ms var(--ease-out), box-shadow 160ms var(--ease-out); } .ds-chip:hover { background: var(--ink); box-shadow: 0 4px 12px oklch(0.2 0.02 40 / 0.4); } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--glaze-bright); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-chip-asking { background: var(--glaze); color: var(--glaze-ink); font-weight: 600; animation: ds-petition 2.4s var(--ease-out) infinite; } .ds-chip-asking:hover { background: var(--glaze-bright); } .ds-chip-done, .ds-chip-done:hover { background: var(--jade); color: var(--jade-ink); } .ds-chip-exited, .ds-chip-exited:hover { background: var(--bone); color: var(--lacquer-deep); } .ds-chip-summon { background: var(--lacquer); padding: 0.375rem 0.75rem 0.375rem 0.625rem; } .ds-chip-summon:hover { background: var(--lacquer-raise); } @keyframes ds-petition { 0% { box-shadow: 0 2px 6px oklch(0.2 0.02 40 / 0.28), 0 0 0 0 oklch(0.8 0.145 82 / 0.7); } 70%, 100% { box-shadow: 0 2px 6px oklch(0.2 0.02 40 / 0.28), 0 0 0 10px oklch(0.8 0.145 82 / 0); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-chip-asking { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
The screen is the court of Hue at a morning audience, seen from the king's side of the glass. Agents are scribes at low writing desks in a paved courtyard. One that needs the user leaves its desk, runs up the central path, and kneels below the throne steps with a yellow petition held over its hat. The scene is the interface: who works and who waits is read from where figures stand and how they hold themselves, before any label is read.

Three grounds hold everything, and each is one material. A vermilion lacquer rail on the left carries the roster. A hazy daylight stage in the middle carries the 3D court. An ink-dark dock on the right, hidden until opened, carries a real terminal or the summon form. Colour is spent like court colour: lacquer is the building, imperial yellow glaze belongs to the roofs and to whatever needs the king, jade is a finished report. Everything else is stone, wood, paper and straw.

The register is an operating tool that stays open for hours beside an editor. Type is small, even and unshouting. Surfaces are flat. Motion is short and exists to report a state change, with one exception that is the signature: a waiting petition keeps calling until it is answered.
keyCharacteristics: One screen, three grounds: lacquer rail, mist stage, ink dock.
State is carried four ways at once: place in the court, posture, icon, colour.
Imperial yellow is the king's colour. In the shell it marks what needs the user and where the user's hand is.
One UI family at three weights; monospace lives only inside the terminal.
Flat surfaces; shadow only under things that float over the scene.
The dock sits beside the scene. Nothing opens as a modal.

rules.name: The King's Yellow Rule
rules.body: In the rail, the chips and the dock, glaze appears only on what needs the king (an asking agent, the primary action, a note to read) and on where the king's hand is (focus ring, caret, selection, the ring under a pointed-at figure). In the scene it is also the roofs, the wall caps and the king's own robe, because that is their material. A courtier's robe, a heading or a decoration never wears it.

rules.name: The Jade Closes Rule
rules.body: Jade means a finished report and nothing else. It is not a general "success" green.

rules.name: The Own-Ink Rule
rules.body: Every filled status colour brings its own text colour: glaze-ink on glaze, jade-ink on jade, lacquer-deep on bone. Bone text never sits on glaze, jade or bone.

rules.name: The Ground Keeps Its Dim Rule
rules.body: Secondary text is bone-dim on lacquer and ink-dim on ink. The two are not interchangeable.

rules.name: The Mono Stays Inside Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only inside the terminal well. Ticket ids, elapsed times and paths in the shell are set in Be Vietnam Pro; numbers that update in place use tabular figures.

rules.name: The Three Weights Rule
rules.body: 400 reads, 500 names, 600 leads. No other weight, no uppercase, no tracked-out labels. The only letter-spacing in the system is -0.01em on the title.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Group headings, labels, buttons and statuses are sentence case in plain words from the court vocabulary ("Before the throne", "At their desks", "Needs your ruling").

rules.name: The Docked, Never Modal Rule
rules.body: The terminal and the summon form open in the dock beside the scene. The court stays visible and live while the user types.

rules.name: The Grouped By Place Rule
rules.body: Lists are grouped by where the agent stands in the court. The scene and the roster always tell the same story in the same order.

rules.name: The Floating Earns Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface gets a shadow only when it is physically over the scene. Anything seated in the rail or the dock is flat.

rules.name: The One Sun Rule
rules.body: The court has one shadow-casting light. Shadow tint is warm ink (hue 40), never neutral black.

rules.name: The Place and Posture Rule
rules.body: A status that matters must be readable with colour removed: the figure is somewhere different and holding itself differently, and its chip and row carry a distinct icon.

rules.name: The Petition Holds Rule
rules.body: The only looping motion in the system belongs to an agent waiting on the user: the chip pulse and the lifted scroll. It does not time out or settle. It ends when the user answers.

rules.name: The One Vocabulary Rule
rules.body: Each status has one label and one icon, defined once and used unchanged by the roster, the chips and the dock.

rules.name: The Two-Press Rule
rules.body: Ending a session arms the same button in place and asks in its label. Destructive actions do not open a dialog.

dos: Do keep every new surface on one of the three grounds: lacquer rail, mist stage, ink dock. Put secondary text in that ground's own dim (bone-dim on lacquer, ink-dim on ink).
Do spend glaze only on what needs the user or on where the user's hand is, with glaze-ink text on it.
Do give every new status a place in the court, a posture, an icon from the court's objects and a label in the shared vocabulary before giving it a colour.
Do use the pill (999px) for anything that floats over the scene or names a status, and the 0.5rem corner for anything that is pressed or typed into.
Do keep type inside the built ramp (1.25, 1, 0.875, 0.8125, 0.75rem) and the three weights (400, 500, 600), in sentence case.
Do draw new icons at 16px with a 1.5px round-capped stroke in the current text colour.
Do time state transitions at 160ms on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` and honour reduced motion by removing travel, loops and pulses while keeping place, posture, icon and colour.
Do tint shadows with warm ink (hue 40) and take scene colours from the scene palette so the court stays one material world.
Do make every figure reachable without the canvas: a real button chip over its head and a real button row in the roster.
donts: Don't use glaze as decoration in the shell, or put a second glaze button on the same ground.
Don't use jade for anything but a finished report, or robe dyes to signal status.
Don't set shell text in JetBrains Mono; it belongs to the terminal well.
Don't use uppercase, letter-spaced labels or a weight outside 400, 500 and 600.
Don't put a shadow, border or gradient between the three grounds while they sit side by side, or a shadow on anything seated in the rail or dock.
Don't open the terminal, the summon form or a confirmation as a modal over the court.
Don't add a second looping animation. The petition is the only thing allowed to keep calling.
Don't signal a state with a coloured dot alone; the court replaces the status-dot dashboard, it does not sit beside one.
Don't let chips overlap or let a petition chip be pushed out of place by a lower-priority one.
